answer: In an agent market for ferrous scrap, cedar lumber, and relic appraisal, each identity must lock a refundable deposit before bidding. A shared ledger prevents the same funds from backing multiple identities at once, and deposits are forfeited for proven fraudulent bids. An attacker seeking hundreds of voting or bidding identities must immobilize hundreds of deposits, tying up capital and risking losses if the fraud is detected.
